- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +15% above recent mean), model often overshoots → cap forecast at +10% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (avg > -0.2), model underestimates downward moves → add 2–5% buffer to forecast for mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in early days (first 5–7 days) → adjust downward by 3–8% for first 7 days if sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment swings from negative to positive, model delays correction → forecast should start rising 2–3 days earlier than sentiment suggests.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive drops), model overestimates recovery → reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 7 days.
